primitives.name: Orinq receipts pallet
primitives.desc: Receipt registry with M-of-N committee attestation, availability certification, anchor records, attestor bonds and slashing, and fee escrow — the on-chain truth every other primitive commits to.

primitives.name: MOTRA fee resource
primitives.desc: Non-transferable transaction-fee resource generated from MATRA holdings (NIGHT/DUST model), charged by a signed extension, with sponsor delegation; the extension also gives a runtime-named (signer, call) set the top transaction-pool priority, one slot per signer, so the guardian's veto cannot be outbid for a place in a block.

primitives.name: Billing pallet
primitives.desc: Application-layer MATRA billing (pay_request) for API calls, metering and attestation evidence — the user-facing spend surface, distinct from MOTRA tx fees.

primitives.name: TEE attestation pallet
primitives.desc: Hardware attestation-evidence registry (secp256r1 and ARM TrustZone phone attestors) binding TEE quotes to receipts.

primitives.name: Committee seating gate
primitives.desc: Composed authority-selection gate: input sanitizer, dead-registered and dead-core liveness filters, seat-ramp clamp, live-quorum floor, growth-slack invariant, break-glass floor and pinned-committee override; refuses (keep-current) rather than seat a committee that cannot finalize.

primitives.name: Main-chain follower
primitives.desc: Cardano main-chain follower backends (db-sync and yaci-store with Mithril-certified stake) supplying candidate registrations and the D-parameter to authority selection.

primitives.name: Mainnet launch preflight
primitives.desc: Fail-closed genesis and launch gate: reads the raw chain spec, the runtime metadata extracted from its code, the authority launch commands (opening sh -c wrappers) and each authority's running node argv from a /proc/<pid>/cmdline capture, the nginx and cloudflared RPC proxy configs, each public RPC URL probed live over HTTP and a WebSocket, and Cardano mainnet through Kupo (the cMATRA genesis lock and its datum, and the permissioned candidates datum). Refuses on a well-known key anywhere (genesis, runtime code, any role or multisig member, the Cardano committee, node configs including dev-phrase URIs and the dev seed, the signing key), Sudo.Key or a genesis account no declared role accounts for, Root not a multisig two keyholders must sign for (one key that meets its threshold alone through a nested multisig counts as one keyholder) or one with a multisig at any depth of more members than the runtime's Multisig.MaxSignatories, which pallet_multisig never signs through, an undeclared off-chain role, a chain spec the anchor worker would read as a test network, attestor or validator reward parameters that are undeclared or not what genesis and the runtime hold, unsafe RPC on an authority, a public RPC URL that lists a method outside the safe set or answers an unsafe one, an authority with no launch entry, under-endowed attestors, genesis storage outside an allowlist, issuance plus the runtime's emission reserves above what the genesis lock holds, a lock fewer than two key holders can spend or not bound to this genesis, PerpEngine under any name, a runtime override or code substitute, a LastRuntimeUpgrade other than the spec version and name build-spec writes for the genesis code, a genesis-enabled Cardano deposit observation with no checkpoint, genesis, code, chain-spec and launch manifest hashes that differ from a manifest signed by a launch key the repo pins, a Root timelock guardian missing from genesis, not the declared multisig, not needing two keyholders or over MaxSignatories by the same test as Root, with a nested multisig member (whose veto the runtime does not take first), the sudo key or sharing any account or member with it, or timelock delays missing, below the runtime's mainnet delays, above its MaxDelay or out of order, both read from the runtime metadata; and hex in the raw spec, the manifests, the launch keys or the key tables in any spelling but the one its writer writes, or a JSON object in them that names a key twice, since the node reads another spelling as other bytes; and a number genesis stores (an attestor reward, the bond, the issuance, an account) at any width but its type's, or an account under any key but its own, which the node reads as zero or never reads; and an authority whose own node binary, pinned by sha256 and captured from its running process, run offline through export-blocks on its running argv's chain and database options, builds another genesis than the one the preflight computes, so any reading of the spec the preflight gets apart from the node shows as another hash, whose --chain names a chain built into the node or a file that is not the checked spec, or that runs another binary than the manifest pins; an authority whose running node serves another genesis as block 0 (its chain_getBlockHash 0, captured from its local RPC), as a node started on a database that already held one or on a spec file overwritten since does; and an authority launch that runs a node subcommand other than build-spec or purge-chain before its node, since the others write a genesis into the base path; and a genesis committee (SessionCommitteeManagement.CurrentCommittee, which the runtime seats at every rotation whose Cardano draw fails, a fresh chain's first among them) that is not exactly the declared authorities' aura and grandpa key pairs, each once, or is longer than the runtime's MaxValidators, genesis Aura and GRANDPA authorities other than the declared keys, each once and every voter at weight 1, session validators other than the committee as the session genesis writes it, a filled pallet_session stub, two authorities that declare one key, a list length in more bytes than parity-scale-codec accepts, or a Cardano permissioned candidate's gran key other than the grandpa key the authority with its aura key declares; and a permissioned candidates datum (read, with the D-parameter, from the one unspent output holding each policy's token, in the formats the node's partner-chains v1.5.1 follower decodes) that holds a candidate Ariadne drops, repeats a key, or holds fewer than the two candidates the runtime draws a committee from, or a D-parameter that seats registered candidates, fewer permissioned seats than candidates, or more than MaxValidators.

primitives.name: Root timelock
primitives.desc: Holds every non-exempt Root call for a per-class delay (recovery for committee toggles and delay raises, the standard delay for everything else including consensus-key levers, sudo key rotation and kill-switch restarts unless the guardian co-signs, long for the dedicated bridge and supply levers) in a bounded vetoable queue with a guardian veto, bulk veto, fast-track and a one-shot advance approval that Root runs without a queue place, plus one guardian change the guardian cannot veto and the sudo key can withdraw; the runtime call filter lets the sudo key reach Root at once only for pause, withdrawal and session-bounded finality break-glass calls, for scheduling and for the approved call, each timelock call is charged for every call its classifier walks, and genesis refuses a chain spec without an independent guardian, or with a development account as guardian, and allows an unguarded one only when its sudo key is a development account or absent. Its mainnet delays (DefaultDelays) and their ceiling (MaxDelay) are metadata constants, so a genesis audit can bound the stored delays from the runtime alone. The guardian's veto and co-sign calls (cancel, cancel_all, fast_track, approve), signed by the current guardian directly or through a multisig as_multi wrapper, are given the top transaction-pool priority through the MOTRA fee extension, bounded to one slot per signer and to the wrapped call's own weight, so a stolen sudo key cannot buy its way past the veto and a compromised guardian cannot use the priority to fill blocks.
